questions.q: In the four-layer sharing model from this lesson, which layer is OWD?
options: The exception layer
The floor
The carve-out layer
The baseline grant
questions.explain: OWD is the floor — the absolute minimum access level before any other mechanism adds to it.

questions.q: A regional sales manager needs to see every Opportunity in their region because they're accountable for the regional forecast. Which layer of the model does this access belong to?
options: Baseline grant
Carve-out
Exception
Floor
questions.explain: Structural access tied to a person's place in the org (and real accountability) is the baseline grant, typically delivered through role or territory hierarchy.

questions.q: An architect finds an object with twelve separate criteria-based sharing rules, each covering a slightly different narrow exception. What does this most often indicate?
options: The object correctly needed twelve distinct exceptions and no redesign is warranted
Apex managed sharing should be added as a thirteenth mechanism
Restriction Rules should replace all twelve sharing rules
The OWD or role hierarchy for that object was likely set incorrectly to begin with
questions.explain: A pile of narrow exceptions is usually a symptom that the baseline (OWD or role hierarchy) doesn't match the real access pattern, pushing work onto the exception layer that belongs one layer up.

questions.q: Per the recommended mechanism ordering in this lesson, when should Apex managed sharing be reached for first?
options: Whenever a public group could also solve the problem, since Apex is more powerful
As the default choice for any new sharing requirement
Only when the sharing logic depends on conditions no declarative tool can express
Whenever the business wants a faster initial build, regardless of long-term maintenance
questions.explain: Apex managed sharing should be the last resort — used only when declarative tools genuinely cannot express the required logic, because it couples visibility to code that must be maintained like everything else.

questions.q: What is the practical test this lesson proposes for whether a sharing design is 'explainable'?
options: Whether every grant can be traced to a one-sentence, nameable business justification
Whether every object in the org uses the same OWD
Whether the design uses Apex managed sharing for at least one object
Whether the design avoids restriction rules entirely
questions.explain: The lesson's explainability test is whether each grant maps to a specific, nameable business reason rather than inherited history nobody wants to touch.
